newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Aug 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Aug 20.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

In the Reserve Bank of Australia's quarterly report, released yesterday, the Bank says it does not believe further cuts in official interest rates are required to stimulate economic growth, as the combination of the latest two cuts with an improvement in the world economy should suffice. Page 1.

Analysts believe rival regional banks may have to work together in areas such as information technology, product development and distribution in order to ensure their long-term survival in the current conditions of the mortgage price war. The predictions follow the release yesterday of a poor profit result from Victoria's Bendigo Bank. Page 1.

Following the release of confidential Federal Government predictions that Australia's energy sector would lift greenhouse gas emissions up to 65 per cent by 2010, Deputy Prime Minister and Trade Minister Tim Fischer said last night Australia's high per capita greenhouse emissions were the result of its energy-intensive exports and its refusal to use nuclear power. Page 3.

The latest American Express Asia Pacific Airfare Index has found Australian airfares have lifted by 8 per cent over the past year, mainly on domestic sectors and on North Asia routes. The Index found business travellers bore the brunt of most of the increases, which were well above inflation figures. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Suggested Federal Government reforms to cut politicians' superannuation schemes have been branded out of step with general community standards by a Senate super committee. It is expected the committee will conclude that pay rises of up to 69 per cent wil be needed to compensate for the cuts. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard announced yesterday the Commonwealth would not support any State or Territory heroin trials, consequently ending plans for Australia's first heroin trial in the Australian Capital Territory. Howard said the decision was made so as not to send the wrong message out to young people about illicit drug use. Page 1.

Canadian adjudicator Anthony Iozzo yesterday found suspected Nazi war criminal Konrad Kalejs should be returned to Australia because of his association with the deaths of thousands of Jews and gypsies in Latvia. Federal Attorney-General Daryl Williams sad the new evidence produced in Canada will be brought back to Australia to investigate whether Kalejs acted against any Australian legislation. Page 1.

Under his crime policy for the Northern Territory election on August 30, Country Liberal Party Chief Minister Shane Stone has announced suspected offenders will lose the long-standing right to remain silent. The proposal is aimed at increasing the power of the Territory's police, and would make it the first jurisdiction in Australia to "remove the veil a criminal can hide behind." Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Under a New South Wales Government overhaul of the final years of schooling to be announced today by Premier Bob Carr and Education Minister John Aquilina, Year 10 students will sit statewide exams in four subjects that will test literacy, numeracy and knowledge of areas such as Australia's political system. Page 1.

Prime Minister John Howard and Federal Cabinet yesterday ended years of efforts by researchers and the Australian Capital Territory Government to gain Commonwealth approval for a heroin trial. Howard feared approving the trial would send the wrong signal out to the community. Page 1.

Environmentalists say a last minute cave-in by NSW Cabinet to irrigators over the issue of the amount of water that should flow to the environment has gutted plans for a A$117 million water reform package for the State. Green groups had hoped the package would go ahead to ensure that part of average river flows would be transferred from irrigators to the environment. Page 1.

New South Wales Police Commissioner Peter Ryan yesterday said he was concerned about the acquittal of former detective Said Morgan, who admitted to killing a man accused of molesting his young relatives. Ryan added that he was firmly against the return of Morgan to the police force. Page 1.
THE AGE

In a move that sparked immediate criticism from Australian Capital Territory Chief Minister Kate Carnell, the Victorian Government and drug law reform advocates, Federal Cabinet yesterday blocked plans for the proposed legal heroin trial in the Territory. Prime Minister John Howard said he supported the decision as a father and a politician who is trying to make the best judgement he can. Page 1.

Ann Koimtsidis, whose son Isaac died from a heroin overdose in his bedroom in the family's home, wrote a letter to Prime Minister John Howard pleading with him to allow the Australian Capital Territory's heroin trial to go ahead. Koimtsidis, who blames the system for her son's death, said no doors should be closed on the issue. Page 1.

Former Melbourne resident Konrad Kalejs was yesterday deported from Canada for alleged Nazi war crimes, after the Australian Special Investigations Unit discovered allegations he had taken part in specific "killing operations" in which thousands died during the Holocaust. Page 1.

A Senate committee heard yesterday the Federal Department of Industry, Science and Tourism underspent its Budget in the 12 months to June by A$131.5 million. According to senior officials, most departmental programs received far less than their Budget allocations, with some receiving less than half their allocation. Page A2.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
